tip: Greek stacks negatives: δεν έφαγα τίποτα (den éfaga típota = I didn't eat anything) is literally 'not I-ate nothing' – both words are required.
No 'on' with holidays: πήγαμε διακοπές (pígame diakopés = we went on holiday) – διακοπές attaches straight to the verb.
Booking is closing in Greek: έκλεισα τα εισιτήρια (ékleisa ta eisitíria = I booked the tickets). κλείνω (kleíno) also books tables and hotel rooms.
You phone TO someone: τηλεφώνησα στην εταιρεία (tilefónisa stin etaireía = I called the company) – with nouns, τηλεφωνώ (tilefonó) takes σε (se).
No 'a' before jobs: έγινε γιατρός (égine giatrós = she became a doctor) – professions drop the article after becoming-verbs.
Greek opens the door TO someone: άνοιξες την πόρτα στη γάτα; (ánoixes tin pórta sti gáta = did you open the door for the cat?) – σε (se), not για (gia).
κοιμήθηκα (koimíthika = I slept) looks passive but isn't – sleep, remember and fear only have passive-shaped forms, so their past ends in -θηκα (-thika).
English 'have you met' is plain past in Greek: Γνώρισες; (gnórises) covers both 'did you meet' and 'have you met' – no perfect needed.
μαθαίνω (mathaíno) is both learn and find out: Έμαθες τα νέα; (émathes ta néa = did you hear the news?).
